title: RAIL: Rethinking Auditory Intelligence in Large Audio-Language Models with a CHC-Grounded Benchmark
abstract: arXiv:2606.11260v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Humans process rich auditory environments through various cognitive capabilities such as audio perception, audio reasoning and memory. Despite recent progress in large audio-language models (LALMs), current evaluation remains largely task- or domain-centric, focusing on end performance while ignoring underlying auditory cognitive behaviors. This gap between how auditory cognition is understood in humans and how it is evaluated in LALMs hinders the interpretation of model behaviour in underlying capabilities and limits alignment with human auditory objectives. We introduce RAIL, a human-centric benchmark grounded in the Cattell--Horn--Carroll (CHC) framework, which formalises auditory cognition into five core capabilities, and develops them into structured evaluation tasks with principled data curation and human-aligned evaluation protocols. translated_title: RAIL：基于CHC框架的基准测试重新思考大型音频-语言模型中的听觉智能
translated_abstract: 人类通过多种认知能力（如听觉感知、听觉推理和记忆）来处理丰富的听觉环境。尽管大型音频-语言模型（LALMs）近来取得了进展，但当前的评估仍然主要围绕任务或领域展开，关注最终性能而忽略了底层的听觉认知行为。人类听觉认知的理解方式与LALMs评估方式之间的这种差距，阻碍了对模型底层能力的解释，也限制了与人类听觉目标的对齐。我们提出了RAIL，这是一个以人类为中心的基准测试，建立在卡特尔-霍恩-卡罗尔（CHC）框架的基础上，将听觉认知形式化为五项核心能力，并通过有原则的数据策划和与人类对齐的评估协议，将其发展为结构化的评估任务。对26个LALMs的评估显示，模型在知识相关任务上表现强劲，但在听觉……（摘要内容在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了RAIL——首个基于CHC认知框架、以人类为中心的听觉智能基准，将听觉认知分解为五项核心能力并构建结构化评估任务，对26个大型音频-语言模型的评估揭示了模型在知识类任务上表现强劲但底层听觉认知能力薄弱的问题。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces RAIL, a human-centric benchmark grounded in the CHC cognitive framework that decomposes auditory cognition into five core capabilities with structured evaluation tasks, and its evaluation of 26 large audio-language models reveals strong knowledge-related performance but weak underlying auditory cognitive abilities.
